## Overview:

The PR updates `parseTimeout` in `src/options.ts` to use `Number(value)` instead of base-10 `parseInt`, while retaining the default timeout and positive-value check. This changes accepted input semantics from integer-prefix parsing to general numeric coercion.

Specialist review should focus on contract compatibility: decimals, non-finite values, whitespace, numeric prefixes, and malformed strings may now behave differently because the safe-integer validation was removed.

## Strengths:

- Small, focused implementation change.
- Preserves the existing default timeout and basic non-positive rejection behavior.
- `Number` avoids silently accepting trailing characters as `parseInt` did.

## Minor candidates:

none.

resolvedReview.overview:
This PR rewrites the timeout validation in `parseTimeout` (`src/options.ts`): `Number.parseInt(value, 10)` plus a `Number.isSafeInteger`/positivity guard is replaced with `Number(value)` and a bare `timeout <= 0` check, while the `undefined → 5000` default is preserved. Despite the stated intent to "preserve existing contracts," the removed guard is load-bearing.

The critical regression is that `Number(value)` returns `NaN` for non-numeric input and `NaN <= 0` is `false`, so invalid strings now **return `NaN` instead of throwing** — the validation this function exists to perform is bypassed. `Infinity` and out-of-safe-range values also slip through. A secondary contract change alters results for previously-parseable inputs (`"1e3"`, `"1.5"`, `"0x10"`). All candidates were confirmed empirically against the old and new implementations.

findings.title: [P1] Restore finite/safe-integer validation — NaN and Infinity bypass the guard
findings.body: `Number("abc")` is `NaN` and `NaN <= 0` evaluates to `false`, so the new guard at `src/options.ts:10-11` lets invalid input fall through to `return timeout` instead of throwing `"invalid timeout"`. Verified empirically: `"abc"` (old: throw → new: returns `NaN`), and even previously-accepted input like `"5000ms"` (old: `5000` → new: `NaN`). `"Infinity"` and `"1e400"` also pass and return `Infinity`. Downstream, `setTimeout(fn, NaN)` and `setTimeout(fn, Infinity)` are coerced by Node to a 1 ms delay, so bad configuration silently produces near-immediate timeouts rather than a clear error. The old `Number.isSafeInteger(timeout)` check rejected exactly these; it must be restored (or replaced with an equivalent `Number.isFinite` + safe-integer + positivity check).

findings.title: [P2] Integer parsing contract changed — fractional, hex, and exponent inputs now accepted with different values
findings.body: Replacing `Number.parseInt(value, 10)` with `Number(value)` at `src/options.ts:10` changes results for real inputs while the PR claims contract preservation: `"1e3"` returned `1`, now returns `1000`; `"1.5"` returned `1`, now returns `1.5` (fractional timeouts are no longer rejected); `"0x10"` threw, now returns `16`; `"9007199254740993"` threw, now returns `9007199254740992` (silent precision loss above `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`). The function previously guaranteed a positive safe integer; callers now can receive fractional or precision-lost values. If accepting decimal/exponent notation is intentional, document it and keep an explicit safe-integer bound; otherwise restore integer parsing.

Despite the stated intent to "preserve existing contracts," the removed guard is load-bearing.

# PR Review

**Verdict:** request_changes

## Overview

This PR rewrites the timeout validation in `parseTimeout` (`src/options.ts`): `Number.parseInt(value, 10)` plus a `Number.isSafeInteger`/positivity guard is replaced with `Number(value)` and a bare `timeout <= 0` check, while the `undefined → 5000` default is preserved. Despite the stated intent to "preserve existing contracts," the removed guard is load-bearing.

The critical regression is that `Number(value)` returns `NaN` for non-numeric input and `NaN <= 0` is `false`, so invalid strings now **return `NaN` instead of throwing** — the validation this function exists to perform is bypassed. `Infinity` and out-of-safe-range values also slip through. A secondary contract change alters results for previously-parseable inputs (`"1e3"`, `"1.5"`, `"0x10"`). All candidates were confirmed empirically against the old and new implementations.

## Verification

No verification baseline ran: `pr_review_verify` reported verification is disabled because no user-level `verificationBaselines` are configured (`enabled: false`). Note that when enabled, baselines execute PR code unsandboxed (supervised only at the original POSIX process group; a deliberate `setsid` escape survives) — an external sandbox/container is recommended for untrusted PRs. Instead, semantics were confirmed directly by executing the old and new function bodies side-by-side in Node for a boundary-input matrix (`"abc"`, `"5000ms"`, `"1e3"`, `"0x10"`, `"1.5"`, `"Infinity"`, `"1e400"`, `"9007199254740993"`, `""`).

## Findings

### [P1] Restore finite/safe-integer validation — NaN and Infinity bypass the guard
**Severity:** P1
**Rationale:** `Number("abc")` is `NaN` and `NaN <= 0` evaluates to `false`, so the new guard at `src/options.ts:10-11` lets invalid input fall through to `return timeout` instead of throwing `"invalid timeout"`. Verified empirically: `"abc"` (old: throw → new: returns `NaN`), and even previously-accepted input like `"5000ms"` (old: `5000` → new: `NaN`). `"Infinity"` and `"1e400"` also pass and return `Infinity`. Downstream, `setTimeout(fn, NaN)` and `setTimeout(fn, Infinity)` are coerced by Node to a 1 ms delay, so bad configuration silently produces near-immediate timeouts rather than a clear error. The old `Number.isSafeInteger(timeout)` check rejected exactly these; it must be restored (or replaced with an equivalent `Number.isFinite` + safe-integer + positivity check).
**Location:** `src/options.ts:10-11 RIGHT`

### [P2] Integer parsing contract changed — fractional, hex, and exponent inputs now accepted with different values
**Severity:** P2
**Rationale:** Replacing `Number.parseInt(value, 10)` with `Number(value)` at `src/options.ts:10` changes results for real inputs while the PR claims contract preservation: `"1e3"` returned `1`, now returns `1000`; `"1.5"` returned `1`, now returns `1.5` (fractional timeouts are no longer rejected); `"0x10"` threw, now returns `16`; `"9007199254740993"` threw, now returns `9007199254740992` (silent precision loss above `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`). The function previously guaranteed a positive safe integer; callers now can receive fractional or precision-lost values. If accepting decimal/exponent notation is intentional, document it and keep an explicit safe-integer bound; otherwise restore integer parsing.
**Location:** `src/options.ts:10 RIGHT`

## Lane completeness

All requested lanes completed.

## Strengths and notes

- The change is small, focused, and preserves the `undefined → 5000` default and the positivity check for well-formed numeric strings.
- `Number` is stricter than `parseInt` for trailing garbage in one direction (no silent prefix truncation of e.g. `"12abc"` into `12`), but that benefit is moot while `NaN` escapes the guard entirely.
- **Correctness:** invalid input silently returns `NaN`/`Infinity` — the main blocking defect.
- **Security:** no security-sensitive changes; the lane found nothing.
- **Performance:** no algorithmic or resource regressions beyond the `NaN`/`Infinity` propagation to timer call sites noted in the P1.
